_comment: LDA 实证大数据锚 · 种子数据。corpus=真实器件实测语料（对抗纯 AI 互证）；adversarial=开放对抗性题库（雷③信任墙）。数值为公开 PDK/文献量级的示例种子，须由社区/退休专家/晶圆厂补真实测量语料。

corpus.method: 晶圆级插入损耗实测。原文逐字：'Measured average insertion loss is 0.28 ± 0.02 dB, uniform across an 8-inch wafer.' 该值为**过量损耗**（不含 3.01 dB 理想分光）。
corpus.note: D-66 逐字核实（2026-09-01）：原 golden=3.4 dB 系「含 3 dB 分光的分支插损」，无可溯源出处；且经核实 arXiv:1909.09538 的 -3.05~-3.15 dB 为**仿真值**（原文：'This simulation is shown in Fig. 5'），不可作实证 golden，已排除。现改用 Opt. Express 21, 1310 (2013) 的实测**过量损耗** 0.28±0.02 dB —— 过量损耗才是被真正测量的器件品质指标（3.01 dB 分光为几何必然，非常数待测量）。

corpus.fab_source: Advanced Micro Foundry (AMF) 商用 SOI 平台；二氧化硅埋层条形波导 500x220 nm^2
corpus.citation: F. Garrisi et al., 'Characterization of photon pairs generated by a silicon ring resonator under electrical self-pumping,' arXiv:2011.03273 (2020), DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2011.03273
corpus.method: 谐振透射谱相邻谐振峰间距直接测量（lambda_p=1547.6 nm）。原文逐字：'The resonator has the shape of a racetrack, it is 66.8 um long and its free spectral range (FSR) is 8.6 nm.'
corpus.note: D-66 逐字核实（2026-09-01）：原 golden=9.15 nm 系按 R=10 um 理想环由 FSR=lambda^2/(n_g*L) **反算**所得（L=2*pi*R=62.83 um），并非该 R 的直接测量。现改用文献**实测**值：racetrack L=66.8 um、FSR=8.6 nm（同一文献并由其反演 n_g=4.18）。闭环自洽校验：lambda^2/(n_g*L) = 1547.6^2/(4.18*66800) = 8.59 nm ≈ 实测 8.6 nm。

corpus.device: SOI strip waveguide 500x220 nm^2 (silica buried) — racetrack resonator L=66.8 um
corpus.fab_source: Advanced Micro Foundry (AMF) 商用 SOI 平台；二氧化硅埋层条形波导 500x220 nm^2
corpus.citation: F. Garrisi et al., 'Characterization of photon pairs generated by a silicon ring resonator under electrical self-pumping,' arXiv:2011.03273 (2020), DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2011.03273
corpus.method: racetrack 谐振腔（add-drop）透射谱 FSR 实测反演：n_g = lambda^2/(FSR*L)，L=66.8 um、FSR=8.6 nm、lambda_p=1547.6 nm。原文逐字：'The resonator has the shape of a racetrack, it is 66.8 um long and its free spectral range (FSR) is 8.6 nm, from which we infer that its group index is 4.18.'
corpus.note: D-66 逐字核实（2026-09-01）：原 E-SOI-NEFF-220 声称 n_eff=2.63±0.02 @1550nm，经核实**该值有误** —— 文献与 3 个独立模式求解器一致给出 500x220 SOI TE0 的 n_eff = 2.44~2.46（2.63 实为 lambda≈1.39um 处的取值，差 0.19，远超其自称 ±0.02）。且 n_eff 本身极少直接测量（D-64 定论），未找到任何可公开溯源的 500x220 n_eff 实测出处。故本条**改判为群折射率 n_g 锚**，取同一文献的实测量。

corpus.device: SiOC-coated Si3N4 strip waveguide 1.2x0.3 um^2 — all-pass microring R=100 um
corpus.fab_source: SiOC 涂覆 Si3N4 平台（PECVD SiO2 埋层），n_Si3N4 = 1.9963 @1550 nm
corpus.citation: 'SiOC-Coated Silicon Nitride Platform for Efficient Phase Actuators,' Coatings (MDPI) 10(4), 309 (2020), DOI 10.3390/coatings10040309
corpus.method: all-pass 微环透射谱 FSR 实测反演：R=100 um、耦合段 12 um、周长 640.3 um，实测 FSR=1.61 nm -> n_g=2.2834。原文逐字：'The free spectral range (FSR) measured from the transmission spectra given in Figure 4b was estimated as 1.61 nm that resulted in the effective group index ng = 2.2834.'
corpus.note: D-66 逐字核实（2026-09-01）：原 E-SIN-NEFF-300 声称 500x300 SiO2 包层 SiN 的 n_eff=1.53，未找到可公开溯源的实测出处（文献中同类几何的 n_eff 多为 COMSOL 仿真值，非测量）。故本条**改判为群折射率 n_g 锚**，并**按文献照实改写几何**为 1.2x0.3 um^2 SiOC 涂覆 Si3N4、R=100 um 环 —— golden 与 geometry 严格同源（同一器件的同一测量）。🔴 **D-66 第 7 例（2026-09-03 二次逐字核实修正）**：geometry.n_clad 原标 1.44 **是错的**。原文三处逐字：①'The refractive index of the deposited SiOC film at standard telecom wavelength 1550 nm was measured as n = 2.2'（SiOC 折射率**高于** Si3N4 芯 1.9963，不是低折射率包层）；②'The SiOC/Si3N4 structures were covered by PECVD silica with n = 1.45'（SiOC 层厚 350 nm，其上另有 PECVD silica）；③'Figure 3 ... TE mode ... is leaky and ... stable propagation of TM mode'（TE 在此结构中泄漏，只有 TM 稳定 —— 与本条 polarization=TM 一致）。已据此把 n_clad 由 1.44 改为 2.2 并把 clad 改写为双层描述。⚠️ **本条当前不作为任何锚题的 golden**（BENCHMARK_DEFS 中无引用），仅入库备查；修正属数据完整性整修，不改变任何判决结果。另注：本器件口径**不自洽**（λ²/(FSR·L)=2.3305 ≠ 原文 2.2834），明文禁止拿它做精度判定 —— 需要 Si3N4 n_g 实证对照时改用同文 Figure 5 的**纯净对照组**（无 SiOC，全 silica 包层，n_g=1.9666，λ²/(FSR·L)=1.9667 自洽），见 lda/lda_solver/semivec_mode_solver.py 自校锚③。

corpus.method: Spectral (OSA) insertion-loss measurement on a 1x2 MMI. Abstract verbatim: 'It exhibits extremely low insertion losses of 0.14 dB and 1.2 dB at the wavelengths of 1.55 um and 2 um, respectively...'
corpus.note: DOI resolved via Optics Express. Value 0.14 dB is the on-chip excess/insertion loss at 1.55 um (wavelength-routed device, so no 3 dB splitting penalty). Footprint 293x6 um^2, SOI 340 nm (from abstract). Used as the MMI 1x2 entry.

corpus.fab_source: 220 nm SOI CMOS-compatible process
corpus.method: Optical-spectrum-analyzer measurement of Y-junction transmission. Abstract verbatim: 'Experimental results achieved using a CMOS-compatible silicon photonics process show an excess loss of lower than 0.5 dB for a splitting ratio varied from 0 to -18 dB across the entire C band.'
corpus.note: DOI resolved via Optics Express (open access). Value is an UPPER BOUND ('lower than 0.5 dB'); reported as 0.5 dB. 220 nm SOI, ultra-compact 1.4x2.3 um. Used as the Y-branch entry.

corpus.fab_source: SOI (electron-beam lithography + ICP etching)
corpus.citation: T. Fukazawa, T. Hirano, F. Ohno, T. Baba, Jpn. J. Appl. Phys. 43(2R), 646-647 (2004), DOI 10.1143/JJAP.43.646
corpus.method: Optical transmission measurement of an elliptical-intersection crossing. Abstract verbatim: 'An insertion loss of less than 0.1 dB was achieved at a wavelength of 1.55 um.'
corpus.note: DOI resolved via JJAP/IOP. Value is an UPPER BOUND ('less than 0.1 dB'); reported as 0.1 dB. Used as the waveguide-crossing insertion-loss entry. Wire width ~0.5 um / h~0.22 um representative of the Baba group's photonic-wire process.

corpus.fab_source: SOI, KOH anisotropic wet etching (smooth trapezoidal sidewalls)
corpus.method: Cutback / spectral loss measurement on KOH-etched rib waveguides (rms roughness 1.49 nm). Abstract verbatim: 'The propagation loss of the waveguide is 1.3 dB/cm at wavelength of 1.55 um.'

geometry.cross_section: trapezoidal SOI rib, KOH-etched (rms roughness 1.49 nm)
geometry.note: exact rib width/height not stated in abstract

corpus.note: DOI resolved via IOP/CPI. Value quoted verbatim. This is the multimode (rib) waveguide entry. Exact rib width/height are not given in the abstract; the device is a trapezoidal SOI rib waveguide fabricated by KOH etching (rms roughness 1.49 nm). Geometry values beyond material indices are left generic to avoid fabrication.

corpus.fab_source: SOI, single etch step (subwavelength grating)
corpus.citation: P. J. Bock, P. Cheben, J. H. Schmid, J. Lapointe, A. Delage, S. Janz, G. C. Aers, D.-X. Xu, A. Densmore, T. J. Hall, Opt. Express 18(19), 20251-20262 (2010), DOI 10.1364/OE.18.020251
corpus.method: Cutback / Fabry-Perot loss measurement on SWG wires. Abstract verbatim: 'Experimental measurements indicate a propagation loss as low as 2.1 dB/cm for subwavelength grating waveguides with negligible polarization and wavelength dependent loss...'

geometry.note: SWG pitch/duty per paper Fig. 2 (~period 300 nm); exact values not in abstract

corpus.note: DOI resolved via Optics Express (open access). Value quoted verbatim. This is the subwavelength-grating-waveguide device entry. h_core~220 nm is the standard NRC SWG platform; exact SWG pitch/duty not in abstract.

corpus.fab_source: SOI, single etch step (subwavelength grating)
corpus.citation: P. J. Bock, P. Cheben, J. H. Schmid, et al., Opt. Express 18(19), 20251-20262 (2010), DOI 10.1364/OE.18.020251
corpus.method: Group index measured via Mach-Zehnder interferometer (SWG MZI). Abstract verbatim: 'The measured group index is nearly constant n_g ~1.5 over a wavelength range exceeding the telecom C-band.'

geometry.note: SWG pitch/duty per paper Fig. 2; exact values not in abstract

corpus.note: DOI resolved via Optics Express (open access). Value quoted verbatim. Used as the n_g (group index) entry; also serves as the subwavelength-grating-waveguide device entry alongside E-SWG-BOCK-PL.

corpus.device: SOI diffractive grating coupler with directionality-enhancing Si overlay (Ghent/LETI)
corpus.fab_source: IMEC/Ghent + CEA-LETI, standard CMOS technology
corpus.citation: G. Roelkens et al., 'High efficiency diffractive grating couplers for interfacing a single mode optical fiber with a nanophotonic silicon-on-insulator waveguide circuit,' Appl. Phys. Lett. 92, 131101 (2008), DOI 10.1063/1.2905260
corpus.method: Measured fiber-to-chip coupling. Paper: "55% coupling efficiency at a wavelength of 1.53μm is experimentally demonstrated on devices fabricated using standard complementary metal-oxide semiconductor technology."

geometry.feature: thin crystalline-Si overlay added before grating definition to enhance directionality

corpus.note: Value 0.55 read directly from paper abstract (experimentally demonstrated). Geometry at platform level (220 nm SOI, 2 um BOX + Si overlay concept); exact grating period/etch not re-fetched from full text.

corpus.device: SOI grating coupler with amorphous-Si overlay (Ghent CMOS pilot line)
corpus.fab_source: 200 mm CMOS pilot line, Ghent/imec
corpus.citation: D. Vermeulen et al., 'High-efficiency fiber-to-chip grating couplers realized using an advanced CMOS-compatible silicon-on-insulator platform,' Opt. Express 18, 18278-18283 (2010), DOI 10.1364/OE.18.018278
corpus.method: Measured fiber-to-chip coupling. Paper: "The fabricated fiber couplers show a coupling efficiency of −1.6dB and a 3dB bandwidth of 80nm." (0.69 = 10^(−1.6/10), fraction conversion of the directly measured −1.6 dB.)
corpus.note: −1.6 dB directly measured; converted to 0.69 fraction. Geometry fully read from paper (period 690 nm, etch 70 nm into crystalline Si, 160 nm a-Si overlay, 13° fiber tilt).

corpus.device: SOI grating coupler with gold bottom mirror (BCB wafer bonding, Ghent/St Andrews)
corpus.fab_source: SOI + InP membranes via Benzocyclobutene (BCB) wafer bonding with gold mirror
corpus.citation: F. Van Laere et al., 'Compact and Highly Efficient Grating Couplers Between Optical Fiber and Nanophotonic Waveguides,' J. Lightwave Technol. 25, 151-156 (2007), DOI 10.1109/JLT.2006.888164
corpus.method: Measured fiber-to-chip coupling. Paper: "The measured coupling efficiency to fiber is 69% for SOI grating couplers and 56% for bonded InP membrane grating couplers."
corpus.note: SOI value 0.69 (69%) used; distinct structure from E-GC-ROEL-08 / E-GC-VERM-10 (gold back-mirror not overlay). Geometry at platform level (220 nm SOI, gold/BCB mirror).

corpus.device: SOI carrier-depletion MZM, lateral PN junction, 0.25 um SOI
corpus.fab_source: 0.25 um thick SOI, 3 um buried oxide
corpus.citation: N.-N. Feng et al., 'High speed carrier-depletion modulators with 1.4V-cm VπL integrated on 0.25μm silicon-on-insulator waveguides,' Opt. Express 18, 7994-7999 (2010), DOI 10.1364/OE.18.007994
corpus.method: DC spectral-shift measurement of π-phase-shift voltage-length product. Paper: "We demonstrate a very efficient high speed silicon modulator with an ultralow π-phase-shift voltage-length product VπL = 1.4V-cm." (1 mm device at 6 V reverse bias; 5 mm device gives 1.3 V-cm.)
corpus.note: VπL = 1.4 V·cm quoted directly from paper (1 mm device, 6 V). Also reported 1.3 V·cm (5 mm device).

corpus.device: SOI carrier-depletion MZM, lateral PN junction, 340 nm SOI (SMIC 0.18 um CMOS photonics)
corpus.fab_source: 200 mm SOI, 340 nm top Si, 2 um BOX, SMIC 0.18 um CMOS photonics process
corpus.citation: X. Xiao et al., 'High-speed, low-loss silicon Mach–Zehnder modulators with doping optimization,' Opt. Express 21, 4116-4127 (2013), DOI 10.1364/OE.21.004116
corpus.method: Insertion loss from normalized transmission spectra. Paper: "By normalizing the recorded optical spectra to a pair of reference grating couplers that are the same as those used in the modulators, a DC insertion loss of 1.9 dB is obtained as shown in Fig. 4(a)."
corpus.note: On-chip DC insertion loss 1.9 dB (reference-grating normalized). Total IL including modulation-induced loss ~3.5 dB (paper).

corpus.device: SOI microring modulator, interleaved p-n junction, racetrack add-drop
corpus.fab_source: SOI (500 nm wide, 170 nm high waveguide, 50 nm slab)
corpus.citation: J. C. Rosenberg et al., 'A 25 Gbps silicon microring modulator based on an interleaved junction,' Opt. Express 20, 26411-26423 (2012), DOI 10.1364/OE.20.026411
corpus.method: Electro-optic figure-of-merit (FOM) = VπL from resonance shift. Paper: "A silicon microring modulator utilizing an interleaved p-n junction phase shifter with a VπL of 0.76 V-cm and a minimum off-resonance insertion loss of less than 0.2 dB is demonstrated."
corpus.note: VπL = 0.76 V·cm quoted directly (0 to −1 V swing; 0.84 at 2 V, ~0.64 in low-bias limit).

corpus.device: Ge-on-SOI waveguide PIN photodetector, butt-coupled, 15 um Ge (Paris-Sud/LETI)
corpus.fab_source: Ge epitaxially integrated on SOI rib waveguide (CMOS compatible)
corpus.citation: L. Vivien et al., '42 GHz pin Germanium photodetector integrated in a silicon-on-insulator waveguide,' Opt. Express 17, 6252-6257 (2009), DOI 10.1364/OE.17.006252
corpus.method: Measured photocurrent vs optical power. Paper: "A -3 dB bandwidth of 42 GHz has been measured at a 4V reverse bias with a responsivity as high as 1 A/W at the wavelength of 1.55 μm and a low dark current density of 60 mA/cm2."
corpus.note: Responsivity 1 A/W at 1.55 um, -4 V (external QE ~80%). Directly measured.

corpus.fab_source: Ge-on-Si, C and L band
corpus.citation: J. Osmond, L. Vivien et al., '40 Gb/s surface-illuminated Ge-on-Si photodetectors,' Appl. Phys. Lett. 95, 151116 (2009), DOI 10.1063/1.3243694
corpus.method: Measured RF/optical −3 dB cut-off from S21. Paper: "The measured −3 dB cut-off frequency is as high as 49 GHz under a reverse bias of 5 V at a wavelength of 1.5 μm."
corpus.note: −3 dB BW 49 GHz at -5 V, 1.5 um. Distinct device (surface-illuminated) from E-PD-VIVI-09 waveguide PD.

corpus.device: Ge-on-SOI waveguide photodiode, 1.3 x 4 um^2 (Sandia CMOS-compatible)
corpus.fab_source: Sandia CMOS-compatible silicon photonics process
corpus.citation: C. T. DeRose et al., 'Ultra compact 45 GHz CMOS compatible Germanium waveguide photodiode with low dark current,' Opt. Express 19, 24897-24904 (2011), DOI 10.1364/OE.19.024897
corpus.method: Measured dark current under reverse bias. Paper abstract: "This photodiode has a best-in-class 3 dB cutoff frequency of 45 GHz, responsivity of 0.8 A/W and dark current of 3 nA."
corpus.note: Dark current 3 nA read from paper abstract (directly measured). 45 GHz BW / 0.8 A/W also reported.

corpus.device: Si-contacted lateral Ge PIN waveguide photodetector (IMEC)
corpus.fab_source: IMEC Si photonics platform, 160 nm thin Ge, poly-Si taper
corpus.citation: H. Chen et al., '-1 V bias 67 GHz bandwidth Si-contacted germanium waveguide p-i-n photodetector for optical links at 56 Gbps and beyond,' Opt. Express 24, 4622-4631 (2016), DOI 10.1364/OE.24.004622
corpus.method: Measured opto-electrical 3-dB bandwidth via S21. Paper: "We demonstrate a 67 GHz bandwidth silicon-contacted germanium waveguide p-i-n photodetector operating at −1 V with 6.8 fF capacitance."
corpus.note: 67 GHz at -1 V (1550 nm). Dark current <4 nA, responsivity 0.74 (1550 nm)/0.93 (1310 nm) A/W also reported.

corpus.fab_source: Ge absorber on Si multiplication region, pseudo-planar vertical structure
corpus.citation: F. Fleming et al., 'Surface-normal illuminated pseudo-planar Ge-on-Si avalanche photodetectors with high gain and low noise,' Opt. Express 32, 19449-19457 (2024), DOI 10.1364/OE.521417
corpus.method: Measured photocurrent at 1550 nm. Paper: "At a wavelength of 1550 nm, 50 µm diameter devices show a responsivity of 0.41 A/W at unity gain, a maximum avalanche gain of 101 and an excess noise factor of 3.1 at a gain of 20."
corpus.note: APD; 0.41 A/W is responsivity at unity gain (max avalanche gain 101). Distinct from PIN detectors.

corpus.device: SOI adiabatic microring resonator, LOCOS process, high-Q (Hebrew Univ.)
corpus.fab_source: SOI 220 nm top Si, 2 um BOX, LOCOS (no RIE) waveguide definition
corpus.citation: J. Nijem et al., 'High-Q and high finesse silicon microring resonator,' Opt. Express 32, 7896-7906 (2024), DOI 10.1364/OE.514080
corpus.method: Measured transmission fit for intrinsic Q. Paper: "an ultrahigh intrinsic Q-factor of ∼2 million with a free spectral range (FSR) of 2 nm was achieved, giving rise to a finesse of ∼1100."
corpus.note: Intrinsic Q ~2e6 directly quoted. FSR 2 nm also measured (placed in geometry).

corpus.fab_source: Standard foundry SOI, 220 nm top Si, 2 um BOX, full-etch strip waveguide
corpus.citation: Z. Han et al., 'Design of ultrahigh-Q silicon microring resonators based on free-form curves,' Opt. Express 32, 9553-9561 (2024), DOI 10.1364/OE.515506
corpus.method: Measured transmission for FSR/loaded-Q. Paper: "The MRR was manufactured using a standard process provided by foundry and measured to have an ultrahigh loaded Q factor of 1.86 × 10^6 and a FSR of about 1 nm."
corpus.note: FSR ~1 nm directly quoted (effective radius 20 um, compact). Loaded Q 1.86e6 also measured (in geometry).

corpus.fab_source: Sputtered tantalum (single-crystal α-Ta) on c-plane sapphire; thin Al wiring layer (Device 18 has a thinner Al layer); e-beam lithography + wet etch + piranha clean
corpus.citation: A. P. M. Place et al., 'New material platform for superconducting transmon qubits with coherence times exceeding 0.3 milliseconds', Nat. Commun. 12, 1779 (2021). DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-22030-5
corpus.method: Time-domain energy-relaxation: "To determine T1, we excite the qubit with a π-pulse and measure its decay over time" (Fig. 1c); single-exponential fit gives T1 = 0.36 ± 0.01 ms for the best device (Device 18).
corpus.note: Directly measured T1 of best device = 0.36 ± 0.01 ms (Fig. 1c), extracted from full-text PDF. Average T1 across all 17 devices = 0.23 ms; time-averaged T1 of best device exceeds 0.3 ms. High confidence.

corpus.device: Al planar transmon on Si (thick Al wiring)
corpus.fab_source: Al wiring layer 300 nm (and 500 nm studied) on high-resistivity Si; e-beam lithography; planar transmon (Xmon-like) with λ/4 CPW readout resonator
corpus.citation: Mitigation of interfacial dielectric loss in aluminum-on-silicon superconducting qubits, npj Quantum Inf. 10, 26 (2024). DOI 10.1038/s41534-024-00868-z
corpus.method: Standard time-domain T1 (energy-relaxation) measurement. Best qubit: time-averaged T1 = 270 μs ± 83 μs (±1σ), highest observed 501 μs. Qubit frequencies 2.8–5.0 GHz; readout resonators 6.0–6.8 GHz.
corpus.note: Best qubit time-averaged T1 = 270 ± 83 μs (±1σ), highest 501 μs, from 40+ measured qubits with 150/300/500 nm Al wiring. Directly reported in text/Fig. 1c of the paper. High confidence.

corpus.fab_source: Sputtered Nb film with Ta surface encapsulation (prevents lossy Nb2O5); planar transmon on Si or sapphire; capping is room-temperature compatible
corpus.citation: M. Bal et al., 'Systematic improvements in transmon qubit coherence enabled by niobium surface encapsulation', npj Quantum Inf. 10, 13 (2024). DOI 10.1038/s41534-024-00840-x
corpus.method: Standard T1: qubit driven from |0> to |1> by a calibrated π-pulse, then read after variable delay and fit to single exponential. For one Nb/Ta device, T1 averaged over 10 h = 161 μs with σ = 15 μs (Fig. 3). A separate Geometry-B device (sapphire) reached median 323 μs, best 586 μs.
corpus.note: Quoted average T1 = 161 ± 15 μs (10 h trace) for a Nb/Ta device. Best device T1 = 586 μs (median 323 μs). Substrate of the 161±15 μs device not explicitly labeled in the text (paper uses both Si and sapphire). Value is explicit with σ; confidence high on the number, medium on substrate.

corpus.fab_source: Al/AlOx Josephson junctions; ~100-junction superinductance array; sapphire substrate; housed in 3D copper cavity (7.54 GHz, Q=377) for dispersive readout
corpus.citation: A. Somoroff et al., 'Millisecond Coherence in a Superconducting Qubit', Phys. Rev. Lett. 130, 267001 (2023). DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.130.267001 (arXiv:2103.08578)
corpus.method: Ramsey (two π/2 pulses, no echo): "The coherence time T2* is obtained from the Ramsey sequence of two π/2-pulses separated by a variable time delay... exponentially decaying envelope". Highest recorded T2* = 1.48 ± 0.13 ms.
corpus.note: T2* (Ramsey, no echo) = 1.48 ± 0.13 ms for the highest recorded coherence; 12-h averaged T2* = 1.16 ± 0.05 ms. Average single-qubit gate fidelity 0.99991. Directly measured. High confidence.

corpus.fab_source: Al transmon (planar) with λ/4 readout resonator; frequency-multiplexed single-shot readout; no quantum-limited amplifier
corpus.citation: L. Chen et al., 'Transmon qubit readout fidelity at the threshold for quantum error correction without a quantum-limited amplifier', npj Quantum Inf. 9, 26 (2023). DOI 10.1038/s41534-023-00689-6
corpus.method: Single-shot frequency-multiplexed readout, 140 ns readout time, using a shelving technique + two-tone excitation + machine-learning post-processing. Assignment fidelity 99.5% (two-state), 96.9% (three-state).
corpus.note: Two-state assignment (readout) fidelity = 99.5% (0.995), three-state = 96.9%, achieved without a quantum-limited amplifier. Directly measured via single-shot readout. High confidence.

corpus.device: Al transmon on SOI (Xmon with SQUID)
corpus.fab_source: Al Josephson junction + SQUID loop on silicon-on-insulator; anhydrous HF vapor etch removes buried oxide; λ/4 CPW readout resonator; planar Xmon
corpus.citation: A. J. Keller et al., 'Al transmon qubits on silicon-on-insulator for quantum device integration', Appl. Phys. Lett. 111, 042603 (2017). DOI 10.1063/1.4994661
corpus.method: Circuit-QED dispersive spectroscopy: fq = ωq/2π = 5.652 GHz measured via a 7.143 GHz resonator (dispersive shift χ/2π = 3.5 MHz, anharmonicity η/2π = −300 MHz).
corpus.note: Measured qubit transition frequency fq = 5.652 GHz (same device has T1 = 3.5 μs, T2* = 2.2 μs). Directly measured via dispersive spectroscopy. High confidence.

corpus.fab_source: Same Al/SOI Xmon + λ/4 CPW resonator as E-Q-ALSOI-FREQ
corpus.method: Vacuum qubit–resonator coupling extracted from the dispersive shift: g ≈ −Δχ(1+Δ/η), with Δ = ωq−ωr; gives g/2π = 177 MHz.
corpus.note: Vacuum Rabi coupling g/2π = 177 MHz, derived from the measured dispersive shift (χ/2π = 3.5 MHz) and anharmonicity. Directly computed from measured circuit parameters. High confidence.

corpus.device: Superconducting Nb CPW resonator on suspended SiN membrane
corpus.fab_source: Nb (~125 nm) CPW resonators etched on a ~110 nm SiN layer on high-resistivity Si; bulk Si underneath etched away to form a suspended membrane (aspect ratio ~7.4×10^3). Al used only for airbridges.
corpus.citation: T. Chistolini et al., 'Performance of Superconducting Resonators Suspended on SiN Membranes', Appl. Phys. Lett. 125, 204001 (2024). DOI 10.1063/5.0222680 (arXiv:2405.01784)
corpus.method: Internal quality factor from transmission fit: Qi = δ_i(n̄=1, T=100 mK)^{-1}. Membrane resonators had median Qi = 0.8×10^5 at single-photon power (on-substrate median 1.2×10^5).
corpus.note: Single-photon internal Q (median) = 8.0×10^4 for suspended-membrane resonators, 1.2×10^5 for on-substrate (same chip). Directly measured at 100 mK. Paper reports medians, not error bars; uncertainty set to ~25% as a reasonable magnitude. High confidence on value order.

corpus.fab_source: LPCVD Si3N4, 644 nm tall × 900 nm wide ring waveguide on SiO2; ring radii ~20 µm; telecom C-band
corpus.citation: A. Gondarenko, M. Lipson et al., 'High confinement micron-scale silicon nitride high Q ring resonator', Opt. Express 17, 11366 (2009). DOI 10.1364/OE.17.011366
corpus.method: From resonant transmission: coupled Q = 244,000 with 70% on-resonance transmission → intrinsic Q = 3,000,000 and intrinsic attenuation 0.12 dB/cm. Scattering <0.065 dB/cm, absorption <0.055 dB/cm (Borselli method from resonance shift vs dropped power).
corpus.note: Directly measured intrinsic Q = 3×10^6 (telecom C-band) from ring transmission fit; one ring showed up to 5.4×10^6. No formal error bar; uncertainty set to ~10% magnitude. High confidence.

corpus.fab_source: LPCVD (and PECVD) SiN microring, R = 80 µm, waveguide width 700 nm, coupling gap 400 nm; measured at 852 nm
corpus.citation: J. W. Hinum-Wagner et al., 'Simulation-guided optimization of CMOS-compatible silicon nitride micro-ring resonators: design, fabrication, and wafer-level evaluation', Opt. Mater. Express 15, 2145 (2025). DOI 10.1364/ome.563484
corpus.method: Wafer-level optical characterization of microring transmission; best devices reached intrinsic Q = 4.2×10^5 and a free spectral range of 1.2 nm at 852 nm (Fig. 9, LPCVD-1 wafer, R=80 µm, W=700 nm, gap=400 nm).
corpus.note: Directly measured FSR = 1.2 nm at 852 nm (ring R=80 µm, W=700 nm). Intrinsic Q = 4.2×10^5. No formal error bar; uncertainty set to ~0.05 nm. High confidence.

corpus.fab_source: LPCVD stoichiometric Si3N4, 300 nm thick, 0.6 µm wide strip waveguide on SiO2; cut-back measurement at 940 nm
corpus.citation: A versatile silicon-silicon nitride photonics platform for enhanced functionalities and applications, Appl. Sci. 9, 255 (2019). DOI 10.3390/app9020255
corpus.method: Cut-back measurement (§2.2): "1 (1.5) dB/cm at 940 nm for 300-nm-thick Si3N4 (SiNx respectively)" — i.e., 1 dB/cm for LPCVD Si3N4 and 1.5 dB/cm for PECVD SiNx, both at 940 nm (Table 1).
corpus.note: Directly measured cut-back propagation loss = 1.0 dB/cm for 300 nm-thick LPCVD Si3N4 at 940 nm (PECVD SiNx counterpart 1.5 dB/cm). No formal error bar; uncertainty set to ~0.1 dB/cm. High confidence.

corpus.device: Si3N4 waveguide on sapphire (SiNOS), ~1.35 µm thick
corpus.fab_source: LPCVD stoichiometric Si3N4, up to 1350 nm thick, width 2.2–2.7 µm, single LPCVD step on sapphire (SiNOS)
corpus.citation: S. Martinussen et al., 'Thick waveguides of low-stress stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire (SiNOS)', Opt. Express 32, 36835 (2024). DOI 10.1364/oe.536578
corpus.method: Optical characterization of proof-of-concept waveguides: propagation loss = 0.30 ± 0.01 dB/cm at 1600 nm.
corpus.note: Directly measured propagation loss = 0.30 ± 0.01 dB/cm at 1600 nm for ~1.35 µm-thick LPCVD Si3N4 on sapphire. This is the closest directly-measured value to the requested ~1.2 µm thick-SiN class. High confidence.

corpus.device: Si3N4 grating coupler with bottom DBR
corpus.fab_source: Si3N4 grating coupler with distributed Bragg reflector (DBR) bottom mirror; designed at 1490 nm; CMOS-compatible
corpus.citation: H. Zhang et al., 'Efficient silicon nitride grating coupler with distributed Bragg reflectors', Opt. Express 22, 21800 (2014). DOI 10.1364/OE.22.021800
corpus.method: Fabricated and characterized grating coupler; peak coupling efficiency ≈ −2.5 dB (i.e., 10^(−2.5/10) ≈ 0.56), with 1-dB bandwidth 53 nm.
corpus.note: Peak fiber-chip coupling efficiency ≈ 0.56 (i.e. −2.5 dB) at 1490 nm with a DBR mirror; 1-dB bandwidth 53 nm. Directly measured. Efficiency reported as fraction = 10^(loss_dB/10). High confidence.

corpus.fab_source: Ge-on-Si evanescent waveguide PD, 2 V reverse bias
corpus.citation: M. M. P. Fard, G. Cowan, O. Liboiron-Ladouceur, Opt. Express 24, 27738 (2016), DOI 10.1364/OE.24.027738
corpus.method: Waveguide-coupled responsivity @1550nm (42.5 GHz bandwidth, 3.5 uA dark)

corpus.device: SOI strip waveguide 220nm (200mm platform) at 2 um band
corpus.fab_source: Standard 200 mm SOI photonic platform, 220nm Si
corpus.method: Cut-back propagation loss @~2000 nm (TE, 220nm SOI strip)

corpus.device: Si microring resonator (2 um band), intrinsic Q
corpus.fab_source: Standard 200 mm SOI platform, 220nm Si, 2 um band
corpus.method: Loaded Q up to 1.1e6, intrinsic Q up to 2e6 (ring on low-loss 220nm SOI waveguide)
